abstract: Language models can make personalized recommendations from rich item content, user history, and feedback. However, evaluating many candidates with full-text inputs incurs substantial online computation and limits serving throughput. We introduce DuoLM, a framework for fast and effective personalized recommendation that integrates a compact recommendation model with an efficient serving runtime. An encoder LLM learns compact item representations for offline reuse, while a personalized ranker LLM combines them with user history and feedback for recommendation. We train both models end to end with recommendation supervision and teacher distillation. The runtime further accelerates inference through virtual token IDs for embedding access, shared history computation, and CUDA Graph replay. Benchmark results show that our framework achieves recommendation quality comparable to that of the expert teacher model. On a single H100, it delivers approximately 26,400 candidate scores per second, about $60\times$ the throughput of the teacher served with vLLM and automatic prefix caching.

sections.body: The paper targets two serving problems: reducing online computation without losing quality, and removing per-candidate overhead in request preparation. DuoLM trains a compact encoder LLM and a personalized ranker LLM end to end, using recommendation labels and distillation from a frozen full-text teacher. Item representations are precomputed offline. The runtime adds virtual token IDs, a multi-item scoring path on SGLang that shares history computation across candidates, and CUDA Graph replay. On Books, NDCG@10 is 0.5586 against 0.5440 for the teacher. On Video Games it is 0.5298 against 0.5313. Throughput reaches up to 60.1× and 109.9× that of the teacher served by vLLM and SGLang, respectively.
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.headline: Language-model recommenders must cut online computation and serving overhead, and DuoLM addresses both with compact reusable item vectors and a serving runtime.

sections.body: The encoder LLM maps each item's templated text to its final EOS hidden state. A continuous interface turns that vector into one input embedding for the ranker LLM. The ranker reads the ordered history of item embeddings with their feedback text, then scores each candidate with a shared linear head. Training combines cross-entropy on the observed target with KL distillation from a frozen full-text teacher, and the distillation weight is raised linearly to a final value. After training, item embeddings are precomputed and only the ranker runs online. The multi-item scoring path prefills the history once per request, and attention masks and position IDs keep candidates isolated. The section states that the packed scores equal standalone scores in exact arithmetic.
sections.heading: Method
sections.headline: An encoder turns each item into one reusable vector, a ranker scores candidates from history vectors, and serving shares history computation across candidates.

sections.body: Rating prediction uses 10,000 training users and 1,000 development users, with history lengths of 1, 3, 5 and 10. It is evaluated with NLL, MAEmed, MAEexp, RMSE and RPS. Next-item recommendation uses 50,000 training users per dataset and reports HR@1, HR@10 and NDCG@10 on 5,000 Books users and 3,000 Video Games users. All methods use 0.6B Qwen3 backbones, and the trained full-text teacher is the quality reference. FIE encodes feedback together with item content, while FIR gives feedback to the ranker as text. The default DuoLM uses FIR with one vector per item. Rating baselines are priors, Content kNN, raw Qwen3-0.6B and HLLM-rating. Recommendation baselines are popularity, history similarity, ContentSASRec and HLLM.
sections.heading: Experiment Settings
sections.headline: Experiments use 0.6B Qwen3 backbones on Amazon Books and Video Games against a full-text teacher and other baselines.

sections.body: On rating prediction, DuoLM's average NLL is 0.9263 against the teacher's 0.9233. It has lower expected-rating MAE and RMSE, while the teacher has lower median-based MAE and RPS. On next-item recommendation, DuoLM's NDCG@10 is 0.5586 on Books against 0.5440 for the teacher, and 0.5298 on Video Games against 0.5313. HLLM has higher HR@1 on Books. The section concludes that quality is comparable to the teacher across the evaluated tasks. In the serving table, with 100 candidates per request on one H100, DuoLM reaches 26,403.98 candidate scores per second at concurrency 64. The teacher served by vLLM reaches 439.08 at the same concurrency.
sections.heading: Results and Analysis
sections.headline: DuoLM stays close to the full-text teacher in quality and serves up to 26,403.98 candidate scores per second on one H100.
